correctness.rationale: The renewal equation includes both complete nearest-lattice resetting intervals and the incompletely reset terminal Brownian flight. Exponential killing produces a symmetric Laplace density and the exact lattice-cell transform; the simple analytic dominant renewal pole solves the hyperbolic implicit equation. Expanding through u^6 yields the exact coefficient N(a) in the RESULT. Crucially the root count is not a numerical plot: for b_n=(2n)![a^{2n}]N(a), b4>0, b5..b11<0, all b_n>0 for n>=12 by explicit monotone exponential dominance. For G(z)=N(sqrt(z))/z^4, G'(z)/z^6 is strictly increasing from negative to positive infinity, proving one minimum; G(0)>0, rigorous N(1)<0 and G(∞)>0 force precisely two simple positive zeros. Independent rational coefficient/tail checks and renewal-equation Taylor solves at three a values corroborate the formula.

evidence: The paper gives the exact nearest-site lattice process and effective diffusion coefficient (second cumulant), with first-passage and optimal-rate properties.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general model and lower moments are prior. The independent coefficient-tail sign argument is new content relative to the material read; model/transform not claimed.

originality.rationale: Alston–Bertrand (2024) establishes the same nearest-site reset model and effective diffusion, but not sixth-cumulant root transitions. A closer previously recorded exact counting-field root for a more general asymmetric periodic lattice (internal identifier c991ac64-5238-4cf5-a452-90f6cdcdb988) already specializes to the generating-function relation, so that equation and ordinary Taylor differentiation are *not* novel. Another prior record (88701ce9-5655-49ee-8f08-34795844182a) proves positive fourth cumulant. The original mathematical remainder, subject to literature risk, is the exact twice-changing sign and infinite root-count argument.
